settings.heading: What it does
settings.content:
Sharpens straight-edge knives in a few minutes. The block keeps the blade at a fixed angle while you roll the diamond disc along the edge.

Two angles. 15° for a fine, keen edge on Japanese and thin blades; 20° for a sturdy edge on everyday chef's knives and outdoor knives.

Coarse to fine. Start on the coarse disc to reset a dull edge, then finish on the finer disc. The Complete Kit adds discs up to a polishing grit.

No power, no water. Nothing to soak, plug in or set up.

settings.heading: Specifications
settings.content:
Angles: 15° and 20° (two faces on the magnetic block)

Roller: wood-grain body, stainless steel ends, swap-in sharpening discs

Block: magnetic steel angle faces, non-slip feet

Essential Kit discs: diamond 400 and 1000 grit

Complete Kit discs: diamond 240, 600 and 1000 grit; whetstone 1200; fine 5000; polishing 10000

Works with: straight-edge stainless and carbon steel knives

Not for: serrated knives, scissors, ceramic blades

settings.heading: How to use
settings.content: Wipe the knife clean and dry. Place the blade flat against the magnetic face of the block, edge facing up: 20° for most kitchen knives, 15° for thin Japanese blades. Hold the block with one hand and roll the coarse disc back and forth along the edge, about 20–30 passes for a dull knife. Flip the knife and repeat on the other side. Switch to the finer disc and repeat with 10–15 passes per side. Wipe the blade before use. Keep fingers away from the edge and roll slowly.

settings.heading: The Same Angle, Every Pass
settings.text:
Most home sharpening goes wrong because the angle drifts. Here the knife sits flat on a magnetic block, so the disc meets the edge at the same angle on every pass, even if you've never sharpened a knife before.

Pick 20° for everyday chef's knives or 15° for thin Japanese blades.
settings.note: For straight-edge knives only. Not for serrated knives, scissors or ceramic blades.

settings.q: Will it work on my knives?
settings.a: It works on most straight-edge kitchen and outdoor knives in stainless or carbon steel, including Japanese knives. It is not for serrated knives, scissors or ceramic blades.
Use 20° for most Western chef’s knives and outdoor knives: the edge is sturdier and lasts longer. Use 15° for thin Japanese blades when you want a finer edge. If you are unsure, start with 20°.
A dull kitchen knife usually takes a few minutes: about 20–30 passes per side on the coarse disc and 10–15 on the finer disc. Knives with chips take longer.

settings.q: What is the difference between the kits?
settings.a: The Essential Kit has diamond discs in 400 and 1000 grit, enough to sharpen everyday kitchen knives. The Complete Kit has six discs, from a coarse 240 for damaged edges up to a 10000 polishing disc for a very smooth finish.
No. The magnetic block holds the knife at the angle for you, so you only need to roll the disc along the edge slowly and evenly.

settings.q: Do I need water or oil?
settings.a: No. The discs are used dry. Wipe the blade and the discs with a dry cloth afterwards.
For most home cooks, every few weeks is enough. Between sharpenings, a few light passes on the fine disc keeps the edge going.
